citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have a written and documented program for the environmental enrichment of the multiple species of
birds used for an active protocol involving wild-caught birds being temporarily housed at the facility. Some required
components of the plan were found within the IACUC approved protocol, but there was no plan approved by the attending
veterinarian, according to the facility representative. Failure to develop a written environmental enhancement plan for
birds can negatively impact their health and well-being, causing unnecessary psychological distress.
The registrant must develop, document, and follow a species-appropriate plan for environmental enhancement adequate
to promote the psychological well-being of any birds being used in USDA-covered bird protocols. The plan must be
approved by the attending veterinarian and must be in accordance with the regulations in this subpart and with currently
accepted professional standards. The plan must address all points in section 3.154, which include social grouping,
environmental enrichment, special considerations, restraint devices and exemptions.
***Correct by September 25th, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
